prerequisites: Expression through written and oral communication in technical language of theoretical fundamentals in the field of engineering

learning_outcomes.text: Knows the main renewable energy sources: solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, bioenergy, as well as their characteristics;
Understands the operating principles of renewable energy conversion technologies into electrical and thermal energy;
Identifies the advantages and limitations of renewable sources compared to conventional ones, in economic, technical, and environmental contexts;
Knows the components and configurations of renewable energy systems, including hybrid systems and storage solutions;
Understands legislative, economic, and regulatory aspects related to the use and integration of renewable energies into energy grids;
Knows the concepts of sustainability, energy efficiency, decarbonization, and energy transition.
Analyze available renewable energy resources in a certain area and evaluate their potential for use;
Dimension and propose configurations of renewable energy systems (e.g., photovoltaic panels, thermal collectors, etc.) adapted to a specific application;
Develop a simplified technical-economic study for the implementation of a renewable energy source;
Compare and select the most suitable energy solutions based on technical requirements, costs, resource availability, and environmental impact;
Use energy simulation software or tools to analyze the performance of proposed systems;
Apply concepts of energy efficiency and energy management in the context of using renewable sources.
Assumes responsibility for adopting sustainable energy solutions, in accordance with environmental requirements and legal regulations;
Is capable of working independently or in a team, for the development of projects that integrate renewable energy sources;
Demonstrates a proactive attitude in identifying and supporting green solutions, oriented towards reducing emissions and protecting the environment;
Respects professional ethics, safety, and sustainability principles in the selection and application of energy technologies;
Is prepared to communicate ideas, solutions, and arguments related to renewable energy effectively, in professional or public contexts;
Develops initiative and autonomy in the continuous learning process regarding new trends and innovations in the field of renewable energy.

syllabus_topics: Global and local energy in the context of sustainable development

Solar energy: The sun as an energy source, energy balance at the Earth's surface, characteristics of solar energy, active and passive systems, solar collector, concentrators, power cycles, hot water preparation installations, photovoltaic cells present and future, solar energy storage
Wind energy: Origin and characteristics, present and future, wind energy, power of a wind generator, auxiliary energies, valorization solutions
Hydraulic energy: Potential, technological solutions, economic, social and environmental impact, energy of water currents, small rivers, tides, waves
Geothermal energy: Nature and characteristics of geothermal energy, utilization and exploitation schemes, environmental impact, present and future

Biomass: Potential and availability. Conversion processes, direct combustion, anaerobic conversion, gasification, hydrogen economy, technological installations for biogas production, biofuels, fuel cells, principles, characteristics, present and perspectives
Residual energy sources: Types and energy potentials, available thermal energy, air, soil, groundwater, industrial 'waste' heat, valorization methods, direct and through energy cycles
Heat pumps: Principles, fields of use. Types of heat pumps, cycles, schemes, heat pump installations, comparative analyses, local, centralized, industrial and agricultural applications
Cogenerations installations: Principles, fields of use. Types, cycles, schemes of cogeneration installations, local, centralized, industrial and agricultural applications
Occupational safety notions in the laboratory. Error analysis.
Techno-economic calculation for a solar water heating system
Determination of functional characteristics of a flat plate solar collector
Determination of functional characteristics of an evacuated tube solar collector with heat pipes
Determination of functional characteristics of a hybrid solar collector, photovoltaic-thermal
Heating installation with a heat pump
Make-up lab works. Submission of lab works
teaching_methods: Debates based on Power Point presentations
Discovery learning models facilitated by direct and indirect exploration of reality (experiments, demonstrations, modeling)
Action-based methods such as exercise, practical activities, and problem-solving
Theory exemplification through case studies and real applications
assessment_rules: The final evaluation result for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity. Whole grades from 1 to 10 will be awarded. A grade of 5 certifies the acquisition of minimal learning outcomes and the granting of corresponding study credits. A minimum grade of 5 is required for the exam, laboratory activity, and project activity.
